name: Summit Sheet
tagline: Plan mountain days you'll finish before dark
about: Summit Sheet plans day hikes and mountain days: realistic timings for your pace, kit for the forecast, a go/no-go check, a route card to leave with someone, and a clear head when something goes wrong.
persona: You are a mountain leader: methodical about timings and escape routes, calm about weather, and firm that turning back is a skill.

onboarding.title: Know your timings before you start
onboarding.subtitle: Your pace and experience set every estimate.
bullets: Kit lists matched to the forecast
Route cards to leave with someone

tools.title: Time the route
tools.subtitle: Distance, ascent → realistic timings

inputs.label: Route
inputs.placeholder: Snowdon via Rhyd Ddu, 12 km, 900 m ascent, out and back

tools.prompt: Time {route} starting at {start} in {conditions} for the profile pace and experience, using Naismith's rule with corrections. Table (Leg | km | Ascent | Estimated time | Arrive by | Notes), kv (total moving time, with breaks, latest safe turnaround time, sunset margin), 3 bullets on where the estimate is least reliable, and a callout on the turnaround rule.

tools.title: Kit for the forecast
tools.subtitle: Pack list matched to conditions
tools.prompt: Kit list for {hours} hours out in: {forecast}, for the profile terrain and experience. Checklist grouped by 'On you', 'In the pack' and 'Emergency', a table (Layer | Purpose | Swap if warmer/colder), 3 bullets on the items people skip that matter most in this forecast, and a callout on group-shelter and headtorch rules.

tools.title: Go or no-go?
tools.subtitle: Weather, ground, group → a verdict

inputs.label: Mountain forecast
inputs.placeholder: 70% chance of cloud on summits, 65 km/h gusts, wind chill -5

inputs.label: Plan & group
inputs.placeholder: Crib Goch with a first-timer, 4 people

tools.prompt: Verdict on: {weather} with plan: {plan}. Text verdict in two sentences (go / modify / no-go), then a table (Factor | Reading | Risk | Mitigation), cards for 2 alternative lower-risk plans (meta = km · hours · exposure), and a callout on the conditions that are an automatic no-go.

tools.title: Route card to leave
tools.subtitle: Tell someone where you are

inputs.label: Route & timings
inputs.placeholder: Helvellyn via Striding Edge, start 09:00 from Glenridding, back by 16:00

tools.prompt: Write a route card for {route} with {contacts}: kv (party, start point, route, escape routes, expected return, panic time, call this number if not heard), a quote with the exact message to send the contact, and 5 bullets on what the contact should do at panic time (including asking emergency services for mountain rescue).

tools.title: Incident: what now
tools.subtitle: Injury, lost, benighted

inputs.label: Details & location
inputs.placeholder: ankle, can't weight-bear, on the ridge at ~800 m, 2 of us, phone 40%, 15:30, cloud coming in

tools.prompt: Incident: {what}. Details: {detail}. Steps for the first 10 minutes in order (group safety, then the casualty, then the call), kv (who to call and what to ask for, location to give, casualties and injuries, kit and shelter available, weather, phone battery), a checklist for keeping everyone warm and findable while waiting, and a callout on when self-evacuation is reasonable and when it is not.

disclaimer: Mountain conditions change fast. Check official forecasts, carry navigation you can use, and call emergency services in an incident. This is planning help, not a safety guarantee.
